name: KEEP RIGHT
spec: white vertical rectangle with black legend KEEP RIGHT and an arrow curving right around a black vertical obstruction bar
meaning: Stay to the right of the divider or obstruction ahead.

snippets.back: Slower traffic must keep right, and a driver being overtaken must not accelerate.
Keep right and use the left lane only to pass; on a three-lane highway, treat the far right lane as the slower through lane and the far left lane as the passing lane.
Roundabouts circle one way: slow, yield inside, enter right into gaps, go counterclockwise, no stops or passes, signal exits, loop on a miss; multi-lane rights keep right, straights exit as entered.
If your vehicle struggles up a steep road, pull off at the first safe spot or keep right so others can pass; uphill vehicles have the right-of-way over downhill ones.
Reserve left lanes for overtakes, keep right under three lanes except passes, left turns and left exits, and signal each shift.
A driver being passed should keep right and must not speed up until the other vehicle finishes passing.
A cyclist should keep right as far as safety permits.
Exits take the right lane with signals and ramp speeds, never last-minute, and cruisers plan mile-matched exits, keep right, shun medians and stops, and clear breakdowns within six hours.

result.summary: No snippet describes a KEEP RIGHT sign shape/colour or its obstruction/divider meaning; all snippets discuss general keep-right lane discipline only.
